newsitem.title: ITALY: Berlusconi graft trial has to restart from scratch.
newsitem.headline: Berlusconi graft trial has to restart from scratch.

text.p: A year-long corruption trial of former Italian prime minister Silvio Berlusconi was declared null and void on Thursday and will start again from scratch.
The trial of Berlusconi and others was thrown into disarray earlier this month when presiding judge Carlo Crivelli stepped down in a row over allegations of bias.
Milan court president Filippo Lo Turco said he had accepted Crivelli's request to withdraw from the trial which he ruled will now re-start on February 5 under a new presiding judge, Francesca Manca.
He declared all the 27 hearings in the trial, which began on January 17, 1996, null and void.
"This is a correct and just decision," said Ennio Amodio, one of Berlusconi's lawyers.

Berlusconi, who leads the opposition centre-right Freedom Alliance, has denied charges that he and others in his Fininvest business empire paid bribes to tax inspectors between 1989 and 1991 to obtain favourable audits of company books.
Crivelli's resignation followed an attempt by Berlusconi, his brother Paolo and two other defendants last October to have him removed from the bench on grounds of partiality.

Their application was based on a private exchange between Crivelli and a prosecutor in which the judge spoke of a "carrot and stick" approach to the trial. An appeal court rejected the suit but ruled the remark showed a "serious lapse of style."

In a written statement to the court, Crivelli said the appeal court ruling had undermined his public prestige and allowed the defendants who had challenged his impartiality "to avoid their natural judge and alter the duration of the trial".

Berlusconi's lawyers said after Crivelli stepped down: "All that concerns us is that the trial begins again as soon as possible in a climate as calm as that in other Milanese courts in which the accused are presumed innocent just as the constitution says."
Berlusconi, who was prime minister for seven months in 1994, is already on trial for corruption along with disgraced former Socialist premier Bettino Craxi who is self-exiled in Tunisia.

The media tycoon is accused of acquiescing in payments by Fininvest of 10 billion lire ($6 million) alleged to have been channelled to Craxi through a Fininvest-linked off-shore company, All Iberian, and various Swiss bank accounts.

A committal hearing is also going on in Milan to decide if Berlusconi should stand trial for allegedly setting up an illegal slush fund when Fininvest bought the Medusa film company in 1988. ($=1,608 lire)
